gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-montagu-slab: Montagu Slab reads like a classic serif with some backbone, its downstrokes sturdy and its turns slender. Montagu Slab then sits under Blockletter, whose ruler-straight, constant-width lines make a crisp, drawn-by-hand counterpoint.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-ovo: Squat, pencil-drawn and precise: that is Blockletter, every stroke cut like a router bit. Ovo follows with softly varied strokes and a tall middle band, so paragraphs would move along in an authoritative, easy way.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-domine: Commanding from the first word, Bloody opens with big round bowls. Domine gives it a dignified partner, its strokes ebbing and swelling gently while every curve keeps breathing space, a quality the heading's low-contrast roundness never offers.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-esteban: Big, round and bloody, Bloody makes its bowls impossible to miss. And Esteban stays quiet beside it, a classic serif with only slight contrast, so the heading earns its keep when it runs big and brief.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-faustina: Round, loud and low in contrast: that's Bloody. Faustina, a classic serif with mild thicks and an open-jawed c, takes over the quieter work and lets the heading's heavy bowls stand apart.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-halant: Bloody brings big round bowls and a commanding, low-contrast presence, while Halant counters with a faint thick-thin shift and a towering x-height. Halant keeps the text steady beneath it.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-headland-one: Headland One spaces its letters well apart. Beneath Bloody's big round bowls it brings a faint thick-thin shift and a tall rounded o, which makes the heading look even bolder.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-hedvig-letters-seri: Round, heavy and unmistakably bloody. Hedvig Letters Serif sits next to those big bowls with open-ended curves and a sturdy lowercase, its faint nib-pressure variation feeling classic against the heading's flat, commanding weight.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-lisu-bosa: Bloody carries big round bowls with low contrast and a commanding feel. It does its best work shouting; Lisu Bosa, a text serif with spilling counters and tall sturdy lowercase, does its best work in editorial running text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC is a classic serif with dignified, literary stature, its terminals pulled well back. Marcellus SC can be sized up a touch to use its cast-iron presence beside Bloody's big round bowls.
